Quick technical readout: I pulled the rollout history and config diffs for Summit Health org (org_id: SH-0912). There was an automated rollback of a tier-assignment change in the canary at 07:30 PT — the rollback reverted org-level tier mappings back to the pre-AB config, which inadvertently reinstated a stricter project-level cap for several projects (clinical-nlp-prod among them).

What likely happened:
- Original plan: map Summit org to tier B (generous per-project allowances).
- Rollback result: projects fell back to default project caps (tier C) that are ~4x lower per-minute.
- Combined with client retry logic, this produced a retry storm and 429 cascade; retries increased observed load on the control plane and backend, causing timeouts.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (ordered):
1) Apply temporary project-level override to restore the intended per-minute allowance for clinical-nlp-prod (hotfix). ETA: 20 minutes.
2) Deploy a short-lived global throttle-smoothing rule to drop aggressive client retries (rate-limit-burst window) for Summit origin IPs. ETA: 40 minutes.
3) Postmortem: adjust rollback automation to preserve explicit tier mappings for orgs with manual overrides.

I’m attaching the diff I referenced and a screenshot of the tier mapping.

Root cause summary (preliminary): The automated rollback path for the canary did not re-hydrate explicit org tier mappings for orgs with manual assignments. This caused affected projects to inherit the stricter default project cap. We’ve opened INF-6821 to track the rollback-automation fix and will include a postmortem with timeline and corrective actions.

- Review retry guidance (Aditya) — short-term doc to help client backoff best practices. ETA: 3 days.
